title: The Geopolitics of AI Compliance: How Rules Reshape Global Competition
fullText: Okay, let's jump right into this explainer and uncover what is basically a hidden financial trap being set for European innovation by the EU AI act. So, the other 95% of AI companies in Europe are left splitting the remaining 20%. It is pure market consolidation driven directly by regulation. Part three, the forever cost. Honestly, the upfront fee isn't even the worst part. It's the structure of these obligations that really hurts. The regulation mandates something called postmarket monitoring. What this means is that once you deploy an AI system, you're required to monitor it forever. Not for one year, not until a specific milestone is met indefinitely.
